prerequisites: Knowledge of differential calculus of one variable functions
Knowledge of differential calculus of several variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and classify bilinear forms and real quadratic forms.
Solve, using symbolic and numerical calculation, problems of maximums, minimums and constrained extremes.
Decompose matrices, geometrically interpret the result and apply it to problem solving.
Use basic concepts, results and techniques in affine and Euclidean geometry.
Relate the intuitive concept of rigid body motion (in the plane or in real space) with orthogonal transformations.
Explain the concept and know the usual techniques of least squares fitting.
Solve Advanced Mathematics problems using computer tools.

syllabus_topics: Orthogonality. Relation to rigid body motion.
Calculation of extremes of functions of several variables.
teaching_methods: Online teaching sessions (virtual expository sessions with videos, presentations, instructional texts, self-assessment questionnaires)
Classroom practices/seminars (tutorial work, individual or group exercises and tasks)
Laboratory practices (solving exercises with MatLab software)
Expository classes (in-person, resolving doubts, developing theoretical results, examples)

assessment_methods.method: Weighted average of partial exams or global exam (NC)

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary call is calculated as NF = 0.2 NL + 0.2 NA + 0.5 NC + 0.1 NCv, where NC is the average of partial exams (0.4 P1 + 0.6 P2) or the global exam (PG). To pass, NF must be >= 5, NC >= 3.5, and NL >= 3.5. If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be min(NF, NC, NL). For extraordinary calls, students can retake an written exam for NC and/or a laboratory practice test for NL; the highest grade for each part is kept. If unlawful means are detected, the grade will be 0 points.
